text: The application for type approval of a lamp shall be submitted by the holder of the trade name or mark or by his duly accredited representative.

The application for type approval shall be accompanied by drawings, sufficiently detailed to permit identification of the type and, if applicable, of the category of the lamp, showing geometrically in what position(s) the lamp (and if applicable the rear window) may be mounted on the vehicle.

The drawings accompanying the application shall show the axis of observation to be taken as the axis of reference in the tests (horizontal angle H = 0°, vertical angle V = 0°) and the point to be taken as the centre of reference during the tests.
The drawings accompanying the application shall show the limit of the apparent surface of the function(s).
The drawings accompanying the application shall show the space reserved and the arrangement intended for the approval marking.
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the drawings shall show the module(s) and the space reserved for the specific identification code(s) of the module(s) on the lamp and on the module(s).
condition: in case of replaceable light source module(s)

text: In the case of an interdependent lamp system, the drawings shall show the interdependent lamp or the combination of interdependent lamps that fulfil the relevant requirements.
condition: in the case of an interdependent lamp system

text: In the case of a lamp that may incorporate a vehicle manufacturer logo, the drawings shall show the vehicle manufacturer logo.
condition: if the lamp may incorporate a vehicle manufacturer logo

text: The application shall be accompanied by a brief technical description stating, in case of lamps with replaceable UN approved light sources, the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.
condition: in case of lamps with replaceable UN approved light sources

text: The brief technical description shall state, in case of lamps with replaceable light source module(s), the light source module specific identification code.
condition: in case of lamps with replaceable light source module(s)

text: The brief technical description shall state the make and type of electronic light source control gear(s) or variable intensity control(s), if any, and if not being part of the lamp.
condition: if electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control is used and is not part of the lamp

text: In the case the lamp shall also be approved with LED substitute light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 128, the brief technical description shall state the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.
condition: if the lamp is also to be approved with LED substitute light source(s)

text: In the case a device is intended to be mounted inside the vehicle, the technical description shall contain the specification of the optical properties (transmission, colour, inclination, etc.) of the rear window(s).
condition: if the device is intended to be mounted inside the vehicle

text: In the case of a lamp that may incorporate a vehicle manufacturer logo, the applicant shall confirm by a statement provided by the vehicle manufacturer that the vehicle manufacturer logo is the official appropriate one related to the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer.
condition: if the lamp may incorporate a vehicle manufacturer logo

text: In the case of a type of lamp differing only by the trade name or mark from a type already approved, it is sufficient that the application is accompanied by a declaration by the lamp manufacturer that the type submitted is identical (except in the trade name or mark) with and has been produced by the same manufacturer as the type already approved, the latter being identified by its approval number.
condition: lamp type differing only by trade name or mark from an approved type

text: In the case of a type of lamp differing only by the trade name or mark from a type already approved, the application shall be accompanied by two samples bearing the new trade name or mark or equivalent documentation.
condition: lamp type differing only by trade name or mark from an approved type

text: In the case of a lamp with variable intensity, the application shall be accompanied by a concise description of the variable intensity control, an arrangement diagram and a specification of the characteristics of the system covering the entire range of intensity.
condition: lamp with variable intensity

text: In the case of lamps equipped with non-replaceable filament light source(s) or light source module(s) equipped with non-replaceable filament light source(s), the application shall be accompanied by a report, acceptable to the Authority responsible for type approval, that demonstrates compliance of these non-replaceable filament light source(s) with the requirements as specified in paragraph 4.11 of IEC 60809, Edition 4.
condition: lamps with non-replaceable filament light source(s)

text: If the description specifies, at the discretion of the applicant, that the lamp may be installed on the vehicle with different inclinations of the reference axis in respect to the vehicle reference planes and to the ground, or rotate around its reference axis, these different conditions of installation shall be indicated in the communication form.
condition: if the applicant specifies different installation inclinations or rotation

text: If not otherwise specified for the relevant lamp, the application shall be accompanied by two complete samples of the lamp; for lamps which are not identical but are symmetrical and suitable for mounting one on the left and one on the right side of the vehicle, the two samples submitted may be identical and be suitable for mounting only on the right or only on the left side of the vehicle.
condition: if not otherwise specified for the relevant lamp

text: For a variable-intensity lamp, the application shall be accompanied by a sample of the variable intensity control or a generator providing the same signal(s).
condition: variable-intensity lamp

text: In the case of a lamp which is intended to be mounted inside the vehicle, the application shall be accompanied by a sample plate or sample plates (in case of different possibilities) having the equivalent optical properties corresponding to those of the actual rear window(s).
condition: lamp intended to be mounted inside the vehicle

text: In the case of a reversing projector tested together with the reversing lamp according to paragraph 5.12.1.2. (b), the application shall be accompanied by drawings showing the relative position of the projector and the lamp and the associated measurement report.
condition: reversing projector tested together with the reversing lamp

text: A separate approval is required for each lamp listed in paragraph 1.

When two or more lamps are part of the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, approval may be granted only if each of these lamps satisfies the provisions set out in this Regulation or in another Regulation.
condition: two or more lamps in the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps

text: Lamps not satisfying the provisions of any of those Regulations shall not be part of a unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
If the type of lamp(s) submitted for approval in pursuance of paragraph 3.1. meets the requirements of this Regulation, approval shall be granted.
condition: if the lamp type meets the requirements

text: All the devices of an interdependent lamp system must be submitted for type approval by the same applicant.
condition: interdependent lamp system

text: Notice of approval or of extension or refusal or withdrawal of approval or production definitely discontinued of a type of lamp pursuant to this Regulation shall be communicated to the Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement which apply this Regulation, by means of a form conforming to the model in Annex 1.
An approval number shall be assigned to each type of lamp approved and shall be indicated for each lamp in the communication form in Annex 1.

A Contracting Party may assign the same approval number to light-signalling devices or systems incorporating a number of lamps but shall not assign the same number to another type of lamp of the same function.
The daytime running lamp shall be identified by the symbol RL (paragraph 5.4.).
The front direction indicator lamp shall be identified by the symbol 1, 1a, 1b, 11, 11a, 11b or 11c according to its category (paragraph 5.6.).
The front end-outline marker lamp shall be identified by the symbol AM (paragraph 5.1.).
The front position lamp for category L vehicle shall be identified by the symbol MA (paragraph 5.1.).
The front position lamp shall be identified by the symbol A (paragraph 5.1.).
The manoeuvring lamp shall be identified by the symbol ML (paragraph 5.10.).
The parking lamp (forward and rearward facing) shall be identified by the symbol 77R (paragraph 5.3.).
The rear direction indicator lamp (steady) shall be identified by the symbol 2a and the rear direction indicator lamp (variable) by the symbol 2b (paragraph 5.6.).
The rear direction indicator lamp for category L vehicle shall be identified by the symbol 12 (paragraph 5.6.).
The rear end-outline marker lamp (steady) shall be identified by the symbol RM1 and the rear end-outline marker lamp (variable) by the symbol RM2 (paragraph 5.2.).
The rear fog lamp (steady) shall be identified by the symbol F1 and the rear fog lamp (variable) by the symbol F2 (paragraph 5.9.).
The rear position lamp for category L vehicle shall be identified by the symbol MR (paragraph 5.2.).
The rear position lamp (steady) shall be identified by the symbol R1 and the rear position lamp (variable) by the symbol R2 (paragraph 5.2.).
The rear-registration plate illuminating lamp shall be identified by the symbol L (paragraph 5.11.).
The rear-registration plate illuminating lamp for category L vehicle shall be identified by the symbol LM1 (paragraph 5.11.).
The reversing lamp shall be identified by the symbol AR (the letters A and R may be mingled) (paragraph 5.8.).
The side direction indicator lamp shall be identified by the symbol 5 or 6 according to its category (paragraph 5.6.).
The side marker lamp for all vehicle categories shall be identified by the symbol SM1 (paragraph 5.7.).
The side marker lamp for M1 vehicles shall be identified by the symbol SM2 (paragraph 5.7.).
The central high mounted stop lamp (steady) shall be identified by the symbol S3 and the central high mounted stop lamp (variable) by the symbol S4 (paragraph 5.5.).
The stop lamp for category L vehicle shall be identified by the symbol MS (paragraph 5.5.).
The stop lamp (steady) shall be identified by the symbol S1 and the stop lamp (variable) by the symbol S2 (paragraph 5.5.).
The reversing projector shall be identified by the symbol RP (paragraph 5.12.).

The applicable change index for each lamp (function) shall be 0 under the 00 series of amendments and 1 under the 01 series of amendments for daytime running lamps, front and rear direction indicator lamps (including vehicle category L), front and rear end-outline marker lamps, front and rear position lamps (including vehicle category L), manoeuvring lamps, parking lamps, rear fog lamps, rear-registration plate illuminating lamps (including vehicle category L), reversing lamps, side direction indicator lamps, side marker lamps, stop lamps (including vehicle category L) and central high mounted stop lamps.
The reversing projector shall have change index 0 under the 01 series of amendments and is not available for type approval according to the 00 series of amendments.
Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings shall be clearly legible and indelible.
With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be at least 5 mm.
The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.

The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.; this sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the approval marking shall include a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
condition: lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately

text: The horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of direction indicators of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12.
condition: lamps which cannot be mounted on either side indiscriminately

text: The horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of front or rear position lamps and front or rear end-outline marker lamps.
condition: lamps which cannot be mounted on either side indiscriminately

text: The horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of reversing lamps with reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.
condition: reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps

text: The horizontal arrow shall be directed towards the front of the vehicle in the case of direction indicators of categories 5 and 6 and combined parking lamps.
condition: lamps which cannot be mounted on either side indiscriminately

text: For direction indicators of category 6 an indication "R" or "L" shall be shown on the lamp, indicating the right or left side of the vehicle.
condition: category 6 direction indicators

text: Lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps shall bear the additional letter "D" to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4.
condition: lamps used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps

text: Lamps which are used as part of an interdependent lamp system shall bear the additional letter "Y" to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4.
condition: lamps used as part of an interdependent lamp system

text: On lamps with reduced light distribution (see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3), the approval marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
condition: lamps with reduced light distribution

text: Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.
condition: lamps other than those with non-replaceable light sources

text: Where the lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s), the lamp shall also bear a marking indicating the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).
condition: lamp approved for LED substitute light source(s)

text: Lamps with an electronic light source control gear, a variable luminous intensity control, a secondary operating mode and/or non-replaceable light sources shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
condition: lamps with electronic light source control gear, variable luminous intensity control, secondary operating mode or non-replaceable light sources

text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
condition: replaceable light source module(s) used

text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module, comprising the starting letters "MD" for "MODULE" followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1. and, in case several non-identical light source modules are used, followed by additional symbols or characters.
condition: replaceable light source module(s) used

text: The approval mark in the light source module identification code does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used, but both marks shall be from the same applicant.
condition: replaceable light source module(s) used

text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
condition: replaceable light source module(s) used

text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii) and the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
condition: replaceable light source module(s) used

text: An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
condition: control gear or variable intensity control part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body

text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.

The approval marking as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
If the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
condition: outer lens designed to be separated from the main body

text: In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bears different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
condition: outer lens used for several devices

text: The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a) shall be affixed on the light source module component.
condition: replaceable light source module(s) used

text: Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number may be affixed anywhere on the lamps, provided that it is visible after their installation.
condition: single approval mark used for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps

text: Where a single approval mark is used for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.
condition: single approval mark used for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps

text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
condition: single approval mark used

text: Every modification of a type of lamp shall be notified to the Type Approval Authority which approved the type, which may then consider that the modifications are unlikely to have an appreciable adverse effect and the lamp still complies, or require a further test report from the technical service.
condition: modification of an approved lamp type

text: Confirmation or refusal of approval, specifying the alterations, shall be communicated by the procedure specified in paragraph 3.2.3.1. to the Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying this Regulation.

The Type Approval Authority issuing the extension of approval shall assign a series number for such an extension and inform the other Contracting Parties by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.
condition: extension of approval

text: The conformity of production procedures shall comply with those set out in the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), with the requirements set forth in paragraph 6.
The approval granted may be withdrawn if the requirements in this Regulation are not met.
condition: requirements not met

text: If a Contracting Party withdraws an approval it has previously granted, it shall forthwith notify the other Contracting Parties applying this Regulation by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.
condition: approval withdrawn

text: If the holder of the approval completely ceases to manufacture a lamp approved in accordance with this Regulation, he shall so inform the authority which granted the approval, which shall inform the other Contracting Parties by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.
condition: production definitively discontinued

text: The Contracting Parties applying the Regulation shall communicate to the United Nations Secretariat the names and addresses of the Technical Services responsible for conducting approval tests and of the Type Approval Authorities which grant approval and to which approval forms issued in other countries are to be sent.
Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.

The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in those sections) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, in their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, shall apply to the lamp.

The requirements of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86 pertinent to each lamp and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed shall be applied, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
condition: where verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible

text: The lamps shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.

Type approval of an assembly of two independent lamps as lamp marked "D" shall only be applicable to front and rear position lamps, stop lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, daytime running lamps and direction indicator lamps.
condition: if the lamp is to be approved as an assembly of two independent lamps marked "D"

text: Type approval of an interdependent lamp system as lamps marked "Y" shall only be applicable to front and rear position lamps, stop lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, daytime running lamps and direction indicator lamps.
condition: if the lamp is to be approved as part of an interdependent lamp system marked "Y"

text: Lamps approved as front or rear position lamps are deemed to be also approved as end-outline marker lamps.
Front and rear position lamps which are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated may also be used as end-outline marker lamps.
condition: if the position lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated

text: Position lamps or daytime running lamps reciprocally incorporated with another function using a common light source are permitted only if designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted.
condition: if the position lamp or daytime running lamp is reciprocally incorporated with another function using a common light source

text: A rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp shall either (a) be provided by multiple light sources (for instance a double filament light source), or (b) be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.
condition: if the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp

text: For a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, a note on the option used (multiple light sources or tell-tale indicating failure) shall be made within the communication document.
condition: if the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp

text: If a front position lamp incorporates one or more infrared radiation generators, the photometric and colour requirements for this front position lamp shall be met with and without the operation of the infrared radiation generator(s).
condition: if the front position lamp incorporates one or more infrared radiation generators

text: On request of the applicant, the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of a lamp (function) may incorporate only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components, provided that all requirements for the specific function of this Regulation are fulfilled and conditions (a) to (d) are met.
condition: if the lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo

text: Irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3., only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer is allowed to be incorporated in the lamp.
condition: if the lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo

text: The applicant shall confirm by a statement (see paragraph 3.1.2.2. (f)) that the incorporated logo is the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer.
condition: if the lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo

text: The enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) of the lamp in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
condition: if the lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo

text: Notwithstanding paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, the logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) does not have to be symmetrical by itself.
condition: if the lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo

text: Stop lamps, direction indicator lamps and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.
condition: in a single lamp containing more than one light source

text: In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the following shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution in Annex 3 and, when all light sources are illuminated, the maximum intensities are not exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced.
condition: in a single lamp containing more than one light source, except daytime running lamps, direction indicators of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c, 12 and rear-registration plate illuminating lamps

text: Where the failure provision is met by producing a tell-tale activation signal, a note in the communication form shall state that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.
condition: if option (b) of paragraph 4.6.1.2 is used

text: For daytime running lamps containing more than one light source, in case of failure of any one light source at least one of the following shall apply: (a) the light intensity at the points of standard light distribution defined in paragraph 2.2. of Annex 3 shall be at least 80 per cent of the minimum intensity required; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraph 6.19.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced.
condition: in a single daytime running lamp containing more than one light source

text: Where a daytime running lamp meets the failure provision by producing a tell-tale activation signal, a note in the communication form shall state that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.
condition: if option (b) of paragraph 4.6.1.3 is used

text: For daytime running lamps, the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.1. on grouping of light sources wired in series as one light source shall apply in addition.
condition: in a single daytime running lamp containing more than one light source

text: For direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12 containing more than one light source, a signal for activation of the tell-tale prescribed in paragraph 6.5.8. of Regulation No. 48 or paragraph 6.3.8. of Regulation No. 53 shall be produced on the basis of either option: (a) any one light source has failed; (b) in the case of a lamp designed for only two light sources, the intensity in the axis of reference is less than 50 per cent of the minimum intensity required; or (c) as a consequence of a failure of one or more light sources, the intensity in one of the directions H=0°, V=0°; H=20° outwards, V=+5°; or H=10° inwards, V=0° (paragraph 2.1. of Annex 3) is less than the minimum intensity required.
condition: for direction indicators of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12 containing more than one light source

text: For direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12, the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.1. shall apply in addition.
condition: for direction indicators of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12 containing more than one light source

text: For rear-registration plate illuminating lamps the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.2. do not apply, but the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.1. shall still apply.
condition: in a rear-registration plate illuminating lamp containing more than one light source

text: For stop lamps and position lamps for vehicles of category L, the tell-tale option of paragraph 4.6.1.2. (b) does not apply; the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.1. and paragraph 4.6.1.2. (a) shall still apply.
condition: for stop and position lamps for vehicles of category L containing more than one light source

text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of category R1 shall be fulfilled automatically.
condition: in case of failure of the variable intensity control

text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear end-outline marker lamp category RM2 emitting more than the maximum value of category RM1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of category RM1 shall be fulfilled automatically.
condition: in case of failure of the variable intensity control

text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of category S1 shall be fulfilled automatically.
condition: in case of failure of the variable intensity control

text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S4 emitting more than the maximum value of category S3, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of category S3 shall be fulfilled automatically.
condition: in case of failure of the variable intensity control

text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a direction indicator of category 2b emitting more than the maximum value of category 2a, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of category 2a shall be fulfilled automatically.
condition: in case of failure of the variable intensity control

text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear fog lamp of category F2 emitting more than the maximum value of category F1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of category F1 shall be fulfilled automatically.
condition: in case of failure of the variable intensity control

text: The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 (provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval), and/or light source module(s), and/or non-replaceable light source(s).

In case a light source category or categories or type(s) is restricted for use in lamps on vehicles in use and originally equipped with such lamps, the applicant shall declare that the lamp is only intended for installation on those vehicles, and this shall be noted in the communication form.
condition: if the light source category or type is restricted for use in lamps on vehicles in use

text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.
condition: in case of replaceable UN approved light source(s)

text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, applying the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed.
condition: in case of replaceable UN approved light source(s)

text: Where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed, the light source holder shall also conform to the IEC 60061 holder data sheet relevant to the category of LED substitute light source(s).
condition: where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed

text: Light-signalling devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
The design of a replaceable light source module shall be such that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position and can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
condition: in case of replaceable light source module(s)

text: The design of a replaceable light source module shall be such that it is tamperproof.
condition: in case of replaceable light source module(s)

text: The design of a replaceable light source module shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source.
condition: in case of replaceable light source module(s)

text: The design of a replaceable light source module shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.
condition: in case of replaceable light source module(s)

text: When the replaceable light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall be met.
condition: in case of replaceable light source module(s)

text: All photometric and colorimetric measurements of the lamp shall be made with respect to the conditions of paragraphs 4.8.1.1 to 4.8.1.10, using the methods of measurement given in Annex 3.
All measurements shall be made using standard light sources as specified in R.E.5.
condition: in the case of replaceable UN approved light sources

text: The standard light source(s) shall have a luminous flux value that does not deviate more than 5 per cent from its reference/objective luminous flux value when test voltage is applied.
condition: in the case of replaceable UN approved light source(s) controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control

text: All measurements shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
condition: in the case of a lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s)

text: The photometric measurements shall be made separately, in accordance with each applicable condition set forth in paragraph 4.8., and all separate measurement results shall be added together.
condition: in case of a lamp (function) using light sources which are subject to more than one of the conditions prescribed in paragraph 4.8.

text: The applicant shall provide, if required by the test laboratory, samples allowing to supply the different light source(s) separately.
condition: in case of a lamp (function) using light sources subject to more than one of the conditions of paragraph 4.8. and if required by the test laboratory

text: During photometric measurements, stray reflections shall be avoided by appropriate masking.
The photometric measurements shall be repeated for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.

text: The intensities of direction indicator lamps shall in general be measured with the light source(s) continuously alight.

text: A reversing lamp (AR) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 8.0∙10^1 cd and meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V.
The luminous intensity of a reversing lamp shall not exceed 3.00∙10^2 cd in or above the H-plane.
The luminous intensity of a reversing lamp shall not exceed 6.00∙10^2 cd below the H-plane, down to 5°D.
The luminous intensity of a reversing lamp shall not exceed 8.00∙10^3 cd below 5°D.
Reversing lamps shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by reversing lamps shall be white.
The light emitted by each of the two samples of rear fog lamp supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 11.

condition: category F1

text: The luminous intensity of a rear fog lamp of category F1 (steady) shall not exceed 3.00∙10^2 cd.
condition: category F1

text: A rear fog lamp of category F2 (variable) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 1.50∙10^2 cd and meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-VI.
condition: category F2

text: The luminous intensity of a rear fog lamp of category F2 (variable) shall not exceed 8.40∙10^2 cd.
condition: category F2

text: The area of the apparent surface of the rear fog lamp in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 140 cm2.
The rear fog lamp shall be subjected to the heat resistance test specified in Annex 6.
Rear fog lamps shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by rear fog lamps shall be red.

The intensity of light emitted by the manoeuvring lamp shall not exceed 5.00∙10^2 cd in all directions in which the light can be observed, when installed in any mounting position specified by the applicant.

The manoeuvring lamp must be so designed that the light emitted directly towards the side, the front or the rear of the vehicle does not exceed 5∙10^-1 cd within the angular field from φmin = arctan((1-h)/10) to φmax = φmin + 11.3 (in degrees, h being the mounting height in m), the measurement being limited to a horizontal angle from +90° to -90° with respect to the line which cuts the reference axis and is perpendicular to the vertical longitudinal plane of the vehicle.

Manoeuvring lamps shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by manoeuvring lamps shall be white.

For the approval of a rear-registration plate illuminating lamp, the illuminated area to be occupied by the plate shall be determined and assigned to one of the categories 1a (at least 340 x 240 mm), 1b (at least 520 x 120 mm), 1c (at least 255 x 165 mm, agricultural or forestry tractors), 2a (at least 330 x 165 mm), 2b (at least 440 x 220 mm), 1 (at least 130 x 240 mm, category L) or 2 (at least 200 x 280 mm, category L).

At each of the points of measurement shown in paragraph 3. of Annex 3, the luminance B produced by a rear-registration plate illuminating lamp of categories 1a, 1b, 1c, 2a and 2b shall be at least 2.5∙10^0 cd/m2.
condition: categories 1a, 1b, 1c, 2a and 2b

text: At each of the points of measurement shown in paragraph 3. of Annex 3, the luminance B produced by a rear-registration plate illuminating lamp of categories 1 and 2 shall be at least 2∙10^0 cd/m2.

text: The gradient of the luminance between the values B1 and B2, measured at any two measurement points 1 and 2, of a rear-registration plate illuminating lamp shall not exceed 2 x Bo/cm, Bo being the minimum luminance measured at the various points.

The luminance measurements of the rear-registration plate illuminating lamp shall be made on a diffuse colourless surface with known diffuse reflection factor, having the dimensions of the registration plate or the dimension exceeding one measuring point, with its centre placed in the centre of the positions of the measuring points.
The diffuse colourless surface(s) shall be placed in the position normally occupied by the registration plate and 2 mm in front of its holder.

Luminance measurements of the rear-registration plate illuminating lamp shall be made perpendicularly to the diffuse colourless surface with a tolerance of 5° in each direction at the points shown in paragraph 3. of Annex 3, each point representing a circular area of 25 mm in diameter.
The measured luminance of the rear-registration plate illuminating lamp shall be corrected for the diffuse reflection factor 1.0.

Devices for the illumination of rear-registration plates of categories 1a, 1b, 1c, 2a and 2b shall be so constructed that the whole surface of the plate will be visible within the angles given in Part D of Annex 2.
condition: categories 1a, 1b, 1c, 2a and 2b

text: The manufacturer of the rear-registration plate illuminating lamp shall specify one or more or a field of positions in which the device is to be fitted in relation to the space for the registration plate.

When the rear-registration plate illuminating lamp is placed in the position(s) specified by the manufacturer, the angle of incidence of the light on the surface of the plate shall not exceed 82° at any point on the surface to be illuminated (or on the part of the plate intended to be illuminated by the device concerned, if more than one part), measured from the extremity of the device's illuminating area furthest from the plate surface (the middle point of the furthest edge parallel to the plate, where such an edge exists).

The rear-registration plate illuminating lamp must be so designed that no light is emitted directly towards the rear, with the exception of red light if the device is combined or grouped with a rear lamp.
Rear-registration plate illuminating lamps shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear-registration plate illuminating lamp shall be sufficiently colourless not to cause any appreciable change in the colour of the registration plate.

The intensity of light emitted by the reversing projector shall not exceed 1.20∙10^4 cd within the projection area as defined by the individual specifications of UN Regulation No. 48, when installed in any mounting position specified by the applicant.
Outside the projection area, the reversing projector shall fulfil either condition (a) or condition (b) of paragraph 5.12.1.2.

condition: if option (a) is applied

text: Under option (b), when the projection of the apparent surfaces of the reversing projector and reversing lamp in the direction of the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest circumscribing quadrilateral, or the minimum distance between their facing edges does not exceed 75 mm measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, the reversing projector shall be tested together with the reversing lamp and the integrated luminous intensity shall not exceed the maximum luminous intensity required in Table 10.

text: The colour of light emitted by the reversing projector shall be white.

condition: designed maximum luminous intensity not exceeding 7.00∙10^2 cd as identified in Annex 1

condition: singular lamp

text: Front/rear position lamps of categories MA and MR fitted as a pair shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 20° inboard / 80° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 10° below (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm).
condition: pair of lamps

text: Singular stop lamps of category MS shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 45° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 10° below (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm).
condition: singular lamp

text: Stop lamps of category MS fitted as a pair shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 0° inboard / 45° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 10° below (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm).
condition: pair of lamps

text: Front/rear position lamps of categories A, R1 and R2 shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 80° outboard (20°/80° below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm) and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 15° below (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5°/15° for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm).

Front/rear parking lamps (77R) shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 0° inboard / 45° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 15° below (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm).

High mounted stop lamps of categories S3 and S4 shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 10° inboard / 10° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 10° above / 5° below.

Daytime running lamps (RL) shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 20° inboard / 20° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 10° above / 5° below.

Side direction indicators of category 5 shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 5° (A) / 55° (B), applying to direction A, and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 15° below (15°/5° for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm).

Side parking lamps (a combination of front and rear facing parking lamps) shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 0° / 45°, applying to front and rear, and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 15° below (15°/5° for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm).

Side marker lamps of category SM1 shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° (A) / 45° (B) and minimum vertical angles of 10° above / 10° below (10°/5° for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm).

Side marker lamps of category SM2 shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 30° (A) / 30° (B) and minimum vertical angles of 10° above / 10° below (10°/5° for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm).

The rear-registration plate illuminating lamp shall be such that the whole surface of the plate is visible within the field of visibility angles shown in Figures A2-IV and Table A2-4, relating to the relative positions of the lamp and the space for the registration plate.

The field-of-visibility angles for the rear-registration plate illuminating lamp, which take account of the partial occultation caused by the lamp, must be adhered to in the directions in which there is most occultation.
The rear-registration plate illuminating lamp must be such as to reduce the areas of the plate partly occulted to the minimum strictly necessary.

The minimum intensities given as a percentage of the minimum intensities required in Figures A3-I to A3-XV shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits; the direction H = 0° and V = 0° corresponds to the reference axis passing through the centre of reference.

text: Front and rear position lamps, parking lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, stop lamps (S1, S2 and MS) and direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12 shall meet, in each direction of measurement, the minimum intensities given as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8) in Figure A3-I.
Daytime running lamps shall meet, in each direction of measurement, the minimum intensities given as a percentage of the minimum intensity required (Table 6) in Figure A3-II.
Stop lamps of categories S3 and S4 shall meet, in each direction of measurement, the minimum intensities given as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (Table 7) in Figure A3-III.

Direction indicator lamps of category 6 shall meet, in each direction of measurement on the outer side of the vehicle, the minimum intensities given as a percentage of the minimum intensity required (Table 8) in Figure A3-IV, the direction H = 5° and V = 0° corresponding to the minimum value prescribed in Table 8.
Reversing lamps shall meet, in each direction of measurement, the minimum intensities in cd shown in Figure A3-V.

text: The conformity requirements shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and geometric standpoint if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
With respect to photometric performances, the conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested when testing photometric performances of any lamp chosen at random according to paragraph 4.8.
For a lamp equipped with a replaceable light source, if the photometric test results do not meet the requirements, the tests shall be repeated using another standard light source.
condition: lamp with replaceable light source and test results not meeting requirements

text: In conformity of production, the chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.

For non-replaceable filament light source(s) or light source module(s) equipped with non-replaceable filament light source, at any conformity of production check the holder of the type approval shall demonstrate the use in normal production and show the identification of the non-replaceable filament light source(s) as indicated in the type approval documentation.
condition: lamps with non-replaceable filament light sources

text: For each type of lamp, the holder of the type approval shall carry out at least the conformity tests at appropriate intervals, in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation.

If any sampling shows non-conformity with regard to the type of test concerned, further samples shall be taken and tested, and the manufacturer shall take steps to ensure the conformity of the production concerned.
condition: if sampling shows non-conformity

text: Tests of conformity shall cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics.
Conformity tests shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in this Regulation.

In conformity tests carried out by the manufacturer, equivalent methods may be used only with the consent of the competent authority, and the manufacturer is responsible for proving that the applied methods are equivalent to those of this Regulation.
condition: if equivalent methods are used

text: Test apparatus used for conformity tests shall be regularly calibrated and correlated with measurements made by a competent authority.
In all cases the reference methods shall be those of this Regulation, particularly for administrative verification and sampling.

Samples of lamps shall be selected at random from the production of a uniform batch, and the assessment shall in general cover series production from individual factories; records from several factories for the same type may be grouped only if they operate under the same quality system and quality management.
The sampled lamp shall be subjected to photometric measurements for the minimum values at the points listed in Annex 3 and to verification of the required chromaticity coordinates.

The manufacturer shall carry out a statistical study of the test results and define, in agreement with the competent authority, acceptability criteria such that, with a confidence level of 95 per cent, the minimum probability of passing a spot check in accordance with Annex 5 would be 0.95.
In sampling by an inspector, the conformity requirements shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and geometric standpoint if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

In sampling by an inspector, the photometric conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested if, when testing according to paragraph 4.8 any lamp chosen at random, no measured value deviates from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3.
In sampling by an inspector, for a lamp equipped with a replaceable light source whose test results do not meet the requirements, the tests shall be repeated using another standard light source.
condition: lamp with replaceable light source and test results not meeting requirements

text: In sampling by an inspector, lamps with apparent defects are disregarded.
In sampling by an inspector, the chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.
In the first sampling, four lamps shall be selected at random; the first sample of two is marked A, the second sample of two is marked B.

The conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples A and B (all four lamps) is not more than 20 per cent; if the deviation of both lamps of sample A is not more than 0 per cent the measurement can be terminated.

The conformity of mass-produced lamps shall be contested if the deviation of at least one specimen of samples A or B is more than 20 per cent; the manufacturer shall then be requested to align production and a repeated sampling according to paragraph 3 shall be carried out within two months after the notification.
condition: deviation of at least one specimen of samples A or B more than 20 per cent

text: The samples A and B shall be retained by the Technical Service until the entire CoP process is finished.
condition: conformity contested after first sampling

text: In the first repeated sampling, four lamps shall be selected at random from stock manufactured after alignment; the first sample of two is marked C, the second sample of two is marked D.

The conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples C and D (all four lamps) is not more than 20 per cent; if the deviation of both lamps of sample C is not more than 0 per cent the measurement can be terminated.

If the deviation of at least one specimen of samples C or D is more than 20 per cent but the deviation of all specimens is not more than 30 per cent, conformity shall be contested, the manufacturer shall be requested again to align production, and a second repeated sampling according to paragraph 4 shall be carried out within two months after the notification; samples C and D shall be retained by the Technical Service until the entire CoP process is finished.
condition: deviation more than 20 per cent but not more than 30 per cent

text: If one specimen of samples C or D deviates by more than 30 per cent, the approval shall be withdrawn and paragraph 5 shall be applied.
condition: deviation of one specimen of samples C or D more than 30 per cent

text: In the second repeated sampling, four lamps shall be selected at random from stock manufactured after alignment; the first sample of two is marked E, the second sample of two is marked F.

The conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples E and F (all four lamps) is not more than 20 per cent; if the deviation of both lamps of sample E is not more than 0 per cent the measurement can be terminated.
If the deviation of at least one specimen of samples E or F is more than 20 per cent, conformity shall be contested, the approval shall be withdrawn and paragraph 5 shall be applied.
condition: deviation of at least one specimen of samples E or F more than 20 per cent

text: Where required according to paragraphs 4.1 and 4.2 of Annex 5, approval shall be withdrawn according to paragraph 3.6 of this Regulation.
In the heat resistance test, the rear fog lamp or daytime running lamp shall be subjected to a one-hour test of continuous operation following a warm-up period of 20 minutes.
The ambient temperature during the heat resistance test shall be 23 °C ± 5 °C.

In the heat resistance test, the light source used shall be of the category specified for the lamp and shall be supplied with a current at a voltage such that it gives the specified average power at the corresponding test voltage.
condition: lamps with replaceable light sources

text: For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources (filament light sources and other), the heat resistance test shall be made with the light sources present in the lamp.
condition: lamps with non-replaceable light sources

text: Where only the maximum power is specified, the heat resistance test shall be carried out by regulating the voltage to obtain a power equal to 90 per cent of the specified power.
condition: only maximum power specified

text: The specified average or maximum power for the heat resistance test shall in all cases be chosen from the rated voltage(s) of 6, 12 or 24 V at which it reaches the highest value; for lamps with non-replaceable light sources the test conditions of paragraph 5.4.5 or 5.9.5 shall be applied.

For light sources operated by an electronic control gear to obtain variable luminous intensity, the heat resistance test shall be carried out under the conditions given at minimum 90 per cent of the higher luminous intensity.
condition: light sources operated by electronic control gear for variable luminous intensity

text: After the heat resistance test, once the lamp has been stabilized at the ambient temperature, no distortion, deformation, cracking or colour modification of the lamp shall be perceptible.
In case of doubt after the heat resistance test, the intensity of light of the lamp shall be measured according to paragraph 5 of this Regulation.
condition: in case of doubt after the heat resistance test

text: When the intensity is measured after the heat resistance test, the values shall reach at least 90 per cent of the values obtained before the heat resistance test on the same lamp.
condition: in case of doubt after the heat resistance test

text: Any approval marking arrangement other than the examples in Annex 7 is acceptable only if made in accordance with paragraph 3.3 of this Regulation.

text: For side marker lamps, the additional check shall be made 4 seconds after switch ON, with reference coordinate HV.
condition: depending on the light source technology

text: A lamp (function) using incandescent technology only is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.1 of Annex 8 are compliant.
condition: if the lamp (function) uses incandescent technology only

text: A lamp (function) using LED technology only is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2 of Annex 8 are compliant.
condition: if the lamp (function) uses LED technology only

text: For a lamp (function) using any other light generating technology, the corresponding intensity requirements shall be tested and checked for compliance at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
condition: if the lamp (function) uses a light generating technology other than incandescent or LED only

text: For a lamp (function) using more than one light generating technology, the corresponding intensity requirements shall be tested following the strictest time requirements according to paragraphs 2.1.1 to 2.1.3 of Annex 8 for the combination of them and checked for compliance.
condition: if the lamp (function) uses more than one light generating technology

text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the corresponding minimum intensity requirements of a lamp (function) shall be tested and checked for compliance at all points in time starting at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
condition: in case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour)
